source_facts.summary: NOAA/NCEP implemented AIGEFS v1.0 operationally on 2025-12-17 as a GraphCast-based 31-member AI global ensemble forecasting system.
HGEFS, not AIGEFS alone, is the 62-member hybrid that combines 31 AIGEFS members with 31 operational GEFSv12 members.
Open-Meteo provides an ensemble API for NOAA model outputs but is not identified by NOAA as the developer of AIGEFS.
AIFS Single became operational on 2025-02-25, AIFS ENS became operational on 2025-07-01, and both were upgraded to v2 on 2026-05-12.
Google's public Weather Lab includes multiple models: WeatherNext Graph, WeatherNext Gen, and an experimental cyclone model that generates 50 possible scenarios up to 15 days ahead.
The exact mapping between the secondary label Google FNV3 and Google's public experimental cyclone-model naming requires the original chart legend or source metadata.
On 2026-07-11 the CWA page identified Bavi as 202609 but had not yet populated the final case fields; JMA had not yet listed 2609 in its post-analysis position table.
The claim that AIGEFS won this five-model comparison cannot yet be reproduced without the original chart, common initialization time, tracker method, ensemble statistic, and finalized best track.

taxonomy_definitions.weather_model_provenance: Preserve the model owner, data provider, model/version identifier, initialization source, and forecast kind.
taxonomy_definitions.forecast_cycle_alignment: Compare model guidance only at a common initialization time and common lead hours.
taxonomy_definitions.ensemble_uncertainty_preservation: Retain ensemble spread and member semantics instead of reducing uncertainty to one line.
taxonomy_definitions.single_event_model_verification: Treat a one-storm result as a bounded case and require a declared quantitative scoring method.
taxonomy_definitions.official_warning_authority: Keep official meteorological warnings authoritative over candidate model guidance.

scout_implications.summary: Scout should retain model owner, data provider, model version, initialization time, and deterministic or ensemble semantics for every weather-model evidence item.
Scout should not rank weather models unless forecasts share a common initialization time, verification source, tracker method, and lead-hour set.
Scout should preserve ensemble spread and member count when presenting AIGEFS, AIFS ENS, GenCast, or another probabilistic forecast instead of showing only one representative line.
Scout should label live comparisons provisional and wait for an official post-analysis best track before producing a durable model-performance artifact.
Scout should treat AI and physics-based model tracks as candidate evidence while official CWA or local meteorological-agency warnings remain authoritative for trip decisions.

discussion_questions: Should Scout require model owner, data provider, model version, initialization time, and forecast kind for every model-derived weather evidence item?
Should Scout block a model-winner label when the comparison lacks a common forecast cycle, ensemble definition, tracker method, or finalized best track?
Which combination of common-lead track error, closest approach, passage classification, and ensemble calibration should be used for after-action scoring?
Should all model-performance learning artifacts remain provisional until the official post-analysis best track is published?
